audit.whatIsWrong: The focus ability is Shock Blast and the cooldown block says to 'dodge or E-block it'. The ability that actually decides your all-ins is Thundering Blow, which is never named.
audit.why: Riot's Thundering Blow (Hammer E): 'Deals magic damage to an enemy and knocks them back a short distance' — 20/18/16/14/12/10. A knockback ends an Aegis Assault channel and throws you out of your own commit, and at 20 seconds at rank 1 it is the longest cooldown in the lane against Shield Vault's 13s. Shock Blast is poke you can walk around; Thundering Blow is the button that beats the engage. And Aegis Assault blocks damage, not displacement, so 'E-block it' does not work on the E.
audit.corrected: Bait Thundering Blow's 20s before committing; the knockback throws you out of the all-in and cancels the channel, and blocking does not stop it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The stance swap is described only as him having 'both stances'. Its two on-swap effects are absent, and one of them is aimed straight at you.
audit.why: Riot's Mercury Cannon/Mercury Hammer: the swap is on 6 seconds, and 'the first attack in this form reduces the target's Armor and Magic Resist' going to Cannon, while the first attack in Hammer form 'deals additional magic damage'. So the swap animation is the burst tell — _missing-interactions.json flags it as his auto-attack reset — and buying armour is worth less than it looks, because his opener shreds it.
audit.corrected: Swapping stances is a 6s auto-attack reset and the first attack after it shreds your armour and MR — the swap animation is your cue to step back.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and both of Jayce's key abilities have six ranks rather than five, which changes how fast they come down.
audit.why: Shock Blast 16/14/12/10/8/6 and Thundering Blow 20/18/16/14/12/10 — six ranks each, because the stance ultimate is levelled early. Rank 1 Shock Blast at 16s is genuinely punishable; a maxed one at 6s is not, and the same slide happens to the knockback. Lightning Field/Hyper Charge is a flat 10s and the swap is 6s.
audit.corrected: Numbers added, with the rank-1-to-rank-6 slide noted so the early punish window reads as temporary.

audit.why: 53.18% over 1700 games with a chart that gives Jayce four stages including levels 1-3 is the one real tension in this entry — but the prose resolves it the same way the win rate does: Pantheon's edge is the Grand Starfall roam out of a poke lane, not the lane itself. Level 6 reading Pantheon and the first-item row reading Skill match that story.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are your whole game here. At level 1 your point-and-click W stun plus autos is one of the strongest in the game — step up and bully Jayce before he has both stances. The danger is his hammer E knockback: if you W-in carelessly he cannons you away mid-dash, so wait for him to whiff E or burn it for waveclear, then W-stun and dump an empowered Q. Don't trade into his cannon-Q poke from range — close the gap or don't engage at all.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are your whole game here. At level 1 Shield Vault's 600-range leap-stun plus autos is one of the strongest openers in the game — bully Jayce before both stances exist. The danger is Thundering Blow: 20 seconds at rank 1, it knocks you out of your own commit and cancels an Aegis Assault channel, and blocking does not stop a displacement. Wait for him to whiff it or spend it on the wave, then W-stun into the empowered Q.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 this turns into a poke lane you cannot freely farm in — his accelerated cannon Q out-ranges your tap Q, so use Aegis Assault (E) to block the poke when you must walk up to last-hit. At 6 your answer is map pressure, not the 1v1: Grand Starfall leaves this lane to cash your early lead into a kill bot or mid before Jayce comes online. Ping for a gank and W-stun onto his face the instant he steps up to poke without E ready.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 this becomes a poke lane you cannot farm freely in — Shock Blast fired through Acceleration Gate gains range, speed and damage, so face it and let Aegis Assault eat it when you must last-hit. Watch his stance swap: it is a 6-second auto reset, and the first attack after swapping to Cannon shreds your armour and MR. At 6, Grand Starfall out of this lane beats any 1v1 inside it — take the kill bot or mid before he comes online.

edits.before: Your point-and-click W stun and level-1 auto damage are among the best in the game — you win the first exchange before Jayce has both stances.
edits.after: Shield Vault's leap-stun and your level-1 auto damage are among the best in the game — you win the first exchange before both stances exist.

edits.before: With his full hammer+cannon combo and Acceleration Gate poke online he can chunk you before you ever reach W range.
edits.after: With Shock Blast fired through Acceleration Gate he chunks you long before you reach Shield Vault's 600 range.

notes: The page was tracking the wrong ability. Shock Blast is poke you can face and block; Thundering Blow is the 20-second knockback that throws you out of your own commit and cancels an Aegis Assault channel — and Aegis Assault blocks damage, not displacement, so the page's 'dodge or E-block it' advice does not transfer to it. I retargeted the cooldown block, the dos, the donts and the interactions row onto Thundering Blow but left focus.text on Shock Blast, since the focus letter is Q and changing both text and letter felt like more surgery than the evidence demands — worth the user's call. Also note both Q and E have SIX ranks here because the stance ultimate is levelled early, so the punish window at 16s and 20s shrinks to 6s and 10s faster than a normal matchup.
